correctness.rationale: The stationary forward equations imply constant current; bounded speeds and finite total mass force the current to be zero, after which a scalar integrating factor gives the unique density up to normalization. The displayed exponent has exponential tails even at g=0 because γ0v1>0. On x>0 its derivative has sign A−Fρ(ux). For 0<ρ≤2, the log derivative of Kρ is bounded below by 2 tanh(t)(1−sech(2t))>0, using monotonicity of a/sinh(2at); for ρ=0 only the strictly increasing B cosh²(t) remains. Thus the center comparison gives the exact half-line sign pattern, including equality. At equality the positive coefficient B+Cρ(4−ρ²)/3 of t² in Fρ gives a strictly negative quartic leading term in log p(x)−log p(0). For each ρ>2 the constructed M0 has positive derivative at s=0, so a small b>0 gives strict signs −,+,− from center to tail, and analyticity plus reflection gives the claimed strict peaks. The rational witness factors with its two displayed roots; it illustrates rather than proves the continuum boundary.
